subject: Discovery: embeddings + rerank for Atlas Analytics — qualification & next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom@atlas-analytics.com>, Lexi Chen <lexi@atlas-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: embeddings + rerank for Atlas Analytics — qualification & next steps

Hi Tom and Lexi,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Short recap of what I heard and suggested next steps so we have alignment: 

Pain points / goals we captured:
- Relevance drop on reranked results for long-tail queries (users seeing stale or off-topic hits).
- Index growth risk: current candidate set is ~120M vectors and expected to reach ~300M in 12–18 months.
- Latency SLO: p95 retrieval+rerank target is 120ms for web queries; internal API budget is 50–80ms for high-value paths.
- Cost pressure: want to avoid >$X/token-equivalent in inference spend — need batching/caching guidance.

Current stack (what you described):
- Embeddings: nightly batch generation (in-house TF embeddings), stored as float32 vectors.
- Vector DB: Faiss index + Postgres metadata; web service sits on EC2 behind an autoscaled pool.
- Reranker: small cross-encoder hosted on a single-node GPU for high-quality ranks, ~8ms/token in current infra.

Success criteria for pilot / POC:
- Demonstrate matched-quality vs current reranker (no worse than 1% MRR drop)
- Achieve p95 end-to-end < 150ms on representative query mix
- Show unit-cost savings via batching/caching or more efficient kernels (target 20–35% reduction)

Immediate next steps we agreed:
1) You to share index size details (shards, average vector dim, growth rate) + a small anonymized sample (CSV) so we can run a quick embed/distance sanity check.
2) We’ll run an internal footprint estimate and return a short benchmarking plan (we aim to surface a 1–2 page proposal).
3) 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra engineer to map data flow and SSO/network constraints — propose Wed or Thu next week.

Attaching a lightweight benchmarks overview and a draft MAP (mutual action plan) — these are placeholders so we can lock dates and owners.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise, can you send the index sample and confirm Tue/Wed availability for the deep-dive?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood_embed_benchmark_50ms.pdf (PDF, 2 pages), MAP-Atlas-Embeddings.xlsx (Excel sheet)
From: Tom Nguyen <tom@atlas-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lexi Chen <lexi@atlas-analytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: embeddings + rerank for Atlas Analytics — qualification & next steps

Thanks Monica — great summary. Couple clarifications / answers inline: 

- Index shape: current index ~120M vectors, dim=768, stored as float32. We shard by customer cohort; roughly 16 shards today (each ~7–9M vectors). Growth estimate: +12–15M vectors per quarter.
- Sample: I’ll drop a scrubbed CSV (id + embedding) to the shared folder by EOD.
- Reranker: our cross-encoder is a distilled bert variant; inference is on a single V100 today. We see p95 ~110ms when local cache hits but spikes to ~250ms under heavy concurrency.
- Query patterns: 65% short queries (<6 tokens) w/ 1–5 candidate rerank; 15% batch offline reranks (nightly enrichment); 20% long queries / multi-sentence.

Latency flexibility: We can tolerate p95 up to 150ms for most product flows except our checkout/leadflow path (50–80ms target).

I’ll send the sample and a short doc describing our sharding scheme. For deep-dive, Thu (Apr 1) 10:00–10:30 PT works for our infra lead (Amit).

Tom
VP of Search Engineering | Atlas Analytics
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Aditya — forwarding the thread. Quick internal notes:
- Atlas is a mid-market account with fast index growth and strict latency for leadflow.
- They use Faiss + in-house embeddings; likely good candidate for our caching + quantization play.
- Proposed next action: I want a lightweight bench (p95 retrieval + rerank) using our 8-bit quant path and a fallback policy to a smaller cross-encoder. Can you help scope compute and expected cost delta?

If you prefer, we can loop in Karthik for embeddings tuning later.

—Monica

Tom / Lexi — appreciate the quick reply and the shard details. Confirming next concrete steps: 

1) You share scrubbed CSV + shard doc (you mentioned EOD yesterday) — I’ll ping if we don’t see it by 17:00 PT today.
2) Deep-dive scheduled: Thu, 2026-04-01 10:00 PT (Amit + Monica + Aditya) — I’ll send calendar invite and agenda.
3) We’ll deliver a 1–2 page bench plan by Mon, 2026-04-06 with cost estimates (quant + runtime choices).
4) Pilot: propose 4-week pilot focused on web rerank path (A/B test) if bench looks good.

For the bench we’ll need:
- representative query log (anonymized, sample of 10k queries)
- sample embeddings (you said ok)
- current p95 numbers per shard if available

If you want, we can also scope an offline batch-rewrite flow to precompute rerank scores for cold queries to reduce peak latency.

I attached the two files I mentioned earlier (bench overview + MAP draft) — they’re intentionally high-level: review and share any changes.

See you Thu.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
